title: compact-on-write allocator + temperature-aware pager and selective recompression
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory utilization under mixed hot/cold workloads by introducing a compact-on-write allocator and a temperature-aware pager; reduces long-tail eviction spikes and spill I/O for multi-tenant serving.
description:
Motivation: Production workloads observed increased fragmentation and bursty spill events for tenants with highly skewed key temperature distributions. Existing slab allocator keeps allocations in place until eviction, which leads to unusable fragments for long-lived cold keys. The pager triggers coarse-grained spilling that causes I/O bursts and latency SLO violations.

This PR implements two coordinated subsystems: (1) a compact-on-write slab allocator that opportunistically compacts small fragmented regions when a write touches a page, reclaiming contiguous slots without global stop-the-world compaction; and (2) a temperature-aware pager that maintains a lightweight per-tenant temperature histogram and prioritizes spill/coalesce operations for cold clusters while deferring noisy hot clusters. The pager also supports selective recompression for very cold values before spilling to reduce bandwidth.

Key changes (single-line summary): compact-on-write allocator, temperature histogram + pager, selective recompression codec integration, new benchmarks and e2e regression tests, and updated observability for eviction/compaction events.

Small illustrative snippet (compact-on-write allocator):
"When handle_write(page, slot, size) -> if slot.is_fragmented() then coalesce adjacent free slots up to target_run_size and relocate live entries into run using transient buffer; update resident offsets atomically."

Behavioral notes and safety: Compaction is opportunistic and bounded by per-tenant CPU and GC budgets to avoid interfering with token-serving SLOs. The implementation acquires only page-local locks and uses per-page transient buffers to move entries; if budget is exhausted the operation aborts and falls back to existing eviction path. Selective recompression runs inline when network bandwidth > threshold is detected (configurable) and is disabled for encrypted entry payloads to avoid double-encryption issues.

Benchmarks and results: Microbenchmarks were executed on benchmark-lab nodes (A100-based). Representative results (median across 5 runs):
- Mixed workload (90% reads, 10% writes) with hot/cold skew 100:1: tail 99th percentile latency improved from 48ms -> 31ms and spill bytes reduced by 42%.
- Cold-heavy workload (many long-lived cold keys): peak spill I/O reduced by 60% and eviction churn reduced by 35%.
- Memory overhead: transient buffer and histogram add ~1.8% resident working set for our config (tunable per-tenant).

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag `kv_compact_on_write` and pager flag `temp_pager_v1`. Default off for Dedicated/Private during initial rollout. Gradual canary across tenants: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if eviction rate or SLO deviations exceed thresholds.

Related work and references: This builds on prior eviction and spill smoothing work (ENG-1621, PRs implementing soft-spill controllers) but diverges by performing localized compaction on write paths rather than large-scale offline compactors. The temperature histogram is inspired by multi-generational caching heuristics used in other systems but optimized for tenant isolation and low-overhead updates at serving scale.

Migration and compatibility notes: No on-disk format changes. Pager recompression writes are compatible with existing loader path; loader checks codec metadata and decompresses appropriately. If selective recompression is enabled, spilled files include a compact metadata header for codec versioning.

Open items and follow-ups:
- Add an LRU-aware variant of the pager that considers time since last write in addition to temperature buckets (ENG-2045).
- Evaluate hardware-accelerated compression paths (NVMe offload) for very large cold spills.
- Tune thresholds per-tenant automatically using Optimize recommendations.
